newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt shares seen consolidating heady gains.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt shares seen consolidating heady gains.

text.p: German shares were expected to consolidate on Thursday as traders pondered how much further equity prices could climb after seven straight record-setting sessions and a steep decline on Wall Street overnight.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade in the DAX index, was steady in early trade, easing 0.04 points to 4,026.93 after posting small gains at the open.
On Wednesday, the 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 49.46 points at 4,055.86 points, a record closing high.
German shares held up surprisingly well to a 119.88 point decline on Wall Street to 7,842.43.
Traders said the strong dollar, trading around 1.7635 marks in the morning, should continue to help shares as will a psychological support level at 4,000.
"It is rather healthy to have a small correction," one trader said, adding the market was not too worried about 100-plus point swings on the Dow Jones Index.
With little corporate news scheduled on Thursday, maybe the major event will be a Bundesbank news conference at 1015 GMT following its regular council meeting.
Traders roundly expected the central bank to leave rates unchanged at the meeting.

Siemens was the most heavily traded stock in early business after the company said on Wednesday it had formed an alliance with computer netowrking group 3Com Corp to jointly market and develop voice and data networking products.
Siemens shares were up 1.15 marks in morning trade to 110.75.
Building group Bilfinger + Berger Bau AG shares were down 3.50 marks at 75 marks after it said 1997 group output climbed three percent to 9.52 billion marks.
Later in the morning, traders were expecting comments on future results from insurance giant Allianz AG which is holding its annual shareholder meeting on Thursday.
